description: Ground truth for the agent-choice eval (plan 2026-10-24-skill-engine-selection, item C). expect.engine is the engine that ends up rendering. expect.flags lists the accepted routing flags for the answer ('a|b' = alternatives; scoring derives the effective engine from file extension plus flags). expect.alsoOk lists other acceptable file extensions. kind/target feed route(); ref is the faithful .exd graph route() measures; measure names the router measure that must fail; intent marks the one case where the user's wish overrides the router; cue is text the task relies on in SKILL.md.

tasks.prompt: Show how the Order service and the Payment service interact: the Order service calls the Payment service three separate times (authorize, capture and refund), and the Payment service sends a webhook back to the Order service. The Order service also writes to the Orders DB and publishes to the Event bus. Show every call as its own arrow.

tasks.label_source: route(ref/out-parallel.exd) suggests d2 (dense: 1 parallel pair)

tasks.prompt: Document our order handling flow left to right with the full step descriptions as the box labels, exactly as written and not shortened. It starts at Order placed, then Validate the shipping address against the postal service API, then Reserve inventory for every line item in the closest warehouse, then Charge the saved payment method and email the receipt, and ends at Order shipped.
tasks.cue: labels over 40 chars per line
tasks.label_source: route(ref/out-longlabel.exd) suggests d2 (text: 3 long labels)

tasks.prompt: Draw our system as three groups. Frontend: Web app, Mobile app, Admin console. Services: Auth, Orders, Billing, Search. Data: Users DB, Orders DB, Cache. Web app calls Auth, Orders and Search; Mobile app calls Auth and Orders; Admin console calls Billing and Orders. Auth reads Users DB, Orders and Billing both use Orders DB, Search uses the Cache, and Orders calls Billing. Keep the three groups visible.
tasks.cue: > 6 cross-group edges
tasks.label_source: route(ref/out-crossgroup.exd) suggests d2 (cross-linked: 11 cross-group edges)

tasks.prompt: Map our whole platform on one diagram, 28 services: gateway, auth, users, profiles, orders, cart, checkout, payments, invoicing, inventory, catalog, pricing, promotions, search, recommendations, reviews, notifications, email, sms, shipping, tracking, returns, fraud, analytics, reporting, audit, config and scheduler. The gateway fronts auth, users, catalog, cart, checkout and search. Users goes to profiles; catalog goes to pricing then promotions, and to inventory; search goes to recommendations then reviews; cart goes to checkout; checkout goes to orders and payments; payments goes to fraud and invoicing; orders goes to inventory, shipping, notifications and analytics; shipping goes to tracking and returns; notifications goes to email and sms; analytics goes to reporting; audit watches payments and orders; scheduler triggers reporting and config. Do not split it up.
tasks.cue: dense or large graph
tasks.label_source: route(ref/out-large.exd) suggests d2 (large: 28 nodes)

tasks.prompt: Draw our service mesh of six services: Auth, Billing, Catalog, Search, Notify and Audit. Nearly everything talks to everything in both directions: every pair is connected except Audit, which only talks to Auth, Billing and Notify. Draw each connection as one two-way arrow.
tasks.cue: dense or large graph
tasks.label_source: route(ref/out-dense.exd) suggests d2 (dense: 13 edges)
